name: Subconscious
outputs: The cards and files a request needs, ready before it is asked for.

name: Quest Autopilot
description: Quest work runs unasked only when the person allows.
purpose: Run Quest work unasked only when the person allows it.
approach: Ask the hub's Proactivity what is due, from the quest's own settings written as a schedule and the quest's asks pulled as events by a Quest events adapter of Intake Sources, ask the hub's Prioritization (through Quest's ordering arm, which calls the hub's arm for everything generic and adds only Quest's own rules) what matters first among the work waiting, then decide to run or skip before any goal is read or model called, from the quest's budget, the roster day, a pinned clock, backpressure and holds. The work it orders is the asks to answer first, the goals of the periods running (period goals, by horizon then deadline) and the solution whose milestone is next; the day's goals are tasks and are not started by a pass.
out_of_scope: What the pass does once started; when work is due and what matters first, which the hub's Proactivity and Prioritization own, so Quest keeps only its settings, its events and its ordering rules; whether work may be done unasked at all, which Judgment Calls owns.
milestones: 1. Budget, cadence, roster and pinned-clock cases give the expected run or skip.
measures_of_success: Scripted settings and clocks give the expected run or skip for every combination of budget, cadence, roster day and run-now request.
parameters: The quest's daily budget, cadence, roster and clock.
inputs: A quest id and the time.
outputs: Run or skip, with the reason.
effects: None: the decision is read only.
usage_notes: Called before any goal is read or model is called. Due comes from quest_ai_runner.run("proactivity", ...) and the order of waiting work from quest_ai_runner.run("prioritization", ...); nothing here restates either.

name: Quest Intents
description: The person's quests as the standing view of what they are working toward, used to say what the work is for.
purpose: Make the AI work from the person's quests.
approach: Hold the quests and their intents as the view each representative acts from, and frame work with the intent behind it. The goals under an intent are of three levels, each ordered by the hub's Prioritization (Quest's arm calls the hub's and adds only Quest's rules): a solution's milestones (the hub's concept), a quest's period goals (each for a particular solution or strategy on the quest) and the day's goals, which are tasks. One to one: a period goal is a milestone of the solution it is for, linked by Quest's spec_solution_id (a goal's spec_metric_id and metric_target_value are optional, so a goal with no metric value is still a milestone); its order is its milestone's, with no ranking of its own. A goal that names no solution yet is asked about once, never given a second milestone; the day's tasks sit under the period goal they serve.
out_of_scope: Which representative holds a quest (Quest Representatives); remembering conversations (Long-Term Memory); moving the intent forward (Intent Evolution); which quest a message belongs to (Place On A Quest).
milestones: 1. Top-intent grounding is scored on labelled cases from quest-backend.
measures_of_success: One balanced number over carry-through across a representative's quests and intent grounding cases.
outputs: The intent frame for the work.
effects: Reads of quests and conversation notes.
usage_notes: Reached by the flow before context is chosen.

name: Proactivity
outputs: The triggers that are due now, each with why it is due.
